channel.description: Public records and local institutions, daily.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 5, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will have a road closure and lane reduction on Wednesday.
Bentonville schedules road closure and lane reduction for Wednesday. The city of Bentonville announced a lane reduction and road closure will take place on Wednesday.
Bentonville to host Dress for success gala on November 7. Dress for Success Northwest Arkansas will hold its annual Little Black Dress Gala on November 7 in Bentonville. The event will include an evening of glamour, celebration, and fundraising to support economic opportunity.
Bentonville to host Little Sugar MTB race on October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the Big Sugar Classic week.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to accept a grant for the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main Extension. The board is asked to accept a grant from the Walton Family Foundation of up to $6,683,590.00 to help fund the construction of the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main Extension. This project would expand the city's water supply infrastructure.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 3006 SE J St from single-family to neighborhood node. This change would allow for a mix of uses, potentially including small-scale commercial or multi-family housing, in an area currently designated for suburban single-family homes.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what matters the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee can consider and what recommendations it can make to the City Council, and may include the election of officers.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Board to receive updates from the city of Bentonville. This item would inform residents about highlights from the Arkansas Airport Operators Association Conference, the status of Eastside Hangar Development, the selection process for an Airport Board Candidate, and the Aviation Engineering Consulting Contract.
On the Rogers One Time Event agenda: Review of September budget report. The board will review the financial budget report for the museum for the month of September.
Rogers to hold fall tree giveaway on October 24. The city of Rogers will host a tree giveaway through its Foresting the Future program on October 24.
Rogers museum commission to meet on October 8. The Rogers Museum Commission will hold a meeting on October 8, from 4:00 PM to 5:00 PM, at 313 S. 2nd Street.
Frozen berries recalled in Arkansas due to potential e. coli contamination. Frozen berries sold at Walmart and Trader Joe's stores in 30 states, including Arkansas, have been recalled by officials due to potential E. coli contamination.
Pea Ridge Library offers new telescope for public use. The Pea Ridge Community Library now has a telescope available for borrowing, allowing residents to view stars, planets, and galaxies with greater clarity.
Northwest Arkansas Business Journal announces 2026 C-Suite Award winners. The Northwest Arkansas Business Journal has announced its 12th class of C-Suite Award winners, recognizing top executives from various sectors.
Brad Sikorski spearheads McAuley Place construction in Bentonville. Brad Sikorski has led the construction of McAuley Place in Bentonville, a project that will provide affordable housing solutions in Northwest Arkansas.
Alison Nation leads Visit bentonville's digital engagement growth. Alison Nation's leadership at Visit Bentonville has resulted in increased digital engagement and visibility for the city.
Tom Allen involved in Pinnacle Hills area development in Rogers. Tom Allen has been involved in the development of the Pinnacle Hills area of Rogers, including leading development and leasing efforts for The Visionaries, Hunt Ventures’.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 3, 2026
item.description:
The Bentonville Institute of Technology broke ground on its approximately 444,000-square-foot campus at the former Walmart Home Office site.
Bentonville Institute of Technology breaks ground on new campus. Members of the Walton family and over 200 attendees were present at the groundbreaking ceremony for the approximately 444,000-square-foot Bentonville Institute of Technology, located at the former Walmart Home Office.
Bentonville announces downtown street closures. The city of Bentonville provided updates on two street closures near downtown.
Bentonville to host fall tree giveaway. The City of Bentonville will host a Fall Tree Giveaway on October 10, 2026, from 7:30 AM to 10:00 AM at 3200 SW Municipal Dr.
Bentonville Bike Fest to return in 2027. The Bentonville Bike Fest has announced its return in 2027.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Bentonville west defeats Springdale 35-9. Bentonville West secured a 35-9 victory over Springdale, with their offense scoring points early in the game.
On the Bentonville Utility Board agenda: Board to accept a grant for the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main Extension. The board is asked to accept a grant from the Walton Family Foundation of up to $6,683,590.00 to help pay for the construction of the "I" Street Water Supply Transmission Main Extension. This would require a budget adjustment.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 3006 SE J St from suburban single-family to neighborhood node.. This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and potentially some small-scale commercial uses at 3006 SE J St, rather than only single-family homes.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what issues the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee can address and may lead to recommendations for the City Council, potentially affecting how local traffic and signage concerns are handled.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Board to receive updates on city airport matters. The board would be informed about highlights from the Arkansas Airport Operators Association Conference, the status of Eastside Hangar Development, the selection of an Airport Board Candidate, and the Aviation Engineering Consulting Contract.
On the Rogers One Time Event agenda: Museum to present its September budget report. This report would provide an overview of the museum's financial status and spending for the month of September.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 2, 2026
item.description:
The Emerald, a $45.1 million multifamily development, has begun construction in Centerton.
Construction begins on $45.1 million multifamily project in Centerton. Capstone Building Corp. has started construction on The Emerald, a 256-unit, 312,414-square-foot multifamily development in Centerton.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what matters the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee can consider and may lead to recommendations for the City Council, potentially affecting how traffic and signage issues are addressed in the city.
On the Bentonville Airport Advisory Board agenda: Board to receive updates on various city airport matters. This item would inform residents about highlights from the Arkansas Airport Operators Association Conference, the status of Eastside Hangar Development, the selection process for an Airport Board Candidate, and the Aviation Engineering Consulting Contract.
Walmart recalls 4.4 million grill brushes. Walmart has announced the recall of more than 4.4 million Expert Grill brushes due to an ingestion hazard, according to the Consumer Product Safety Commission.
Walmart pasta recall expanded for possible listeria contamination. A recall on pasta sold at Walmart locations nationwide has been expanded due to possible listeria contamination, according to a notice from the Food and Drug Administration.
Centerton to host forum for mayoral and City Council candidates. A candidate forum will be held in Centerton for those running for mayor and City Council.
Siloam springs launches multifamily recycling program. A recent grant will enable Siloam Springs to deploy a new multifamily recycling program.
Northwest Arkansas Community College to host inaugural homecoming festivities. Northwest Arkansas Community College will celebrate its first-ever homecoming, with college officials hoping for a strong start.
Educators discuss early technical training at Bentonville summit. At a Bentonville summit, educators highlighted the importance of early technical training and workforce preparation, noting a shortage of workers in skilled trades.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Northwest Arkansas Land Trust names Marson Nance as new CEO. Marson Nance, a longtime conservation leader, has been named the new CEO of the Northwest Arkansas Land Trust.
Red clay strays added to 2027 Walmart AMP schedule. The Alabama-based country rock band Red Clay Strays has announced new tour dates for 2027, including a stop at the Walmart AMP.
September 2026 was warmest on record for Northwest Arkansas. September 2026 was the warmest September on record for Northwest Arkansas and the River Valley, with temperatures significantly exceeding historical averages.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — October 1, 2026
item.description:
The Willard & Pat Walker Charitable Foundation donated $15 million to Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art to provide free admission to temporary exhibitions.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 3006 SE J St from suburban single-family to neighborhood node.. This proposed change would allow for a mix of housing types and potentially some small-scale commercial uses at 3006 SE J St, rather than only single-family homes.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee can do, including electing officers and making recommendations to the City Council.
Bella Vista to offer free fall trees with sign-up beginning Friday. Bella Vista residents can sign up starting this week to receive a free tree later this month.
Bikes, Blues and BBQ begins in Rogers. The Bikes, Blues and BBQ event kicked off in Rogers on Wednesday night.
Crystal Bridges receives $15 million for free temporary exhibit admission. The Willard & Pat Walker Charitable Foundation donated $15 million to Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art to provide free admission to its temporary exhibitions for visitors 25 and younger, veterans, active-duty military, and SNAP recipients.
Benton County opens new justice center. A new justice center is now operational in Benton County.
SGS bicycle testing company earns Bentonville accreditation. SGS, a bicycle testing company, has received accreditation for its Bentonville lab.
Walmart awards $15 million grant to feeding America. Walmart has awarded a $15 million grant to the Feeding America nonprofit organization.
Scouting America council to honor Hunt family. The Natural State Council of Scouting America will honor the Hunt family at its 2026 Northwest Arkansas Heart of the Eagle luncheon.
Jobless rates decline in most Arkansas metros. Jobless rates in August were lower in six of the seven metro areas in or connected to Arkansas compared with August 2025, with Northwest Arkansas having the lowest rate at 2.9%.
Northwest Arkansas Land Trust CEO Grady Spann retires. Grady Spann, CEO and executive director of the Northwest Arkansas Land Trust, will retire on October 1, and Marson Nance has been promoted to succeed him.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 30, 2026
item.description:
The Benton County Quorum Court has begun its 2027 budget process.
Benton County Quorum Court begins 2027 budget process. The Benton County Quorum Court has started planning for the 2027 fiscal year by reviewing forecasted finances and departmental needs.
Rogers announces road closures for Bikes, Blues & BBQ. The city of Rogers is warning motorists about street closures and traffic changes this week due to the annual Bikes, Blues & BBQ event.
On the Bentonville Planning Commission agenda: Commission to consider rezoning 3006 SE J St from suburban single-family to neighborhood node.. This proposed change would allow for a mix of residential and commercial uses at 3006 SE J St, potentially bringing more services or housing options to the area.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee is responsible for, including the election of officers and potential recommendations to the City Council.
Calara working on $565 million in Benton County housing projects. Calara, the land development arm of Rausch Companies, is under contract for a Bentonville land deal that would create approximately 900 residential lots, part of an estimated $565 million in housing projects in Benton County.
Chamber of mothers expands into Arkansas with new chapters. Chamber of Mothers, a nonpartisan nonprofit focused on maternal health, affordable childcare, and paid leave, has launched chapters in Northwest Arkansas and Little Rock.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Bentonville medical center offers free mammograms. Bentonville Medical Center is partnering with a local breast cancer nonprofit to offer free screenings this week.
Washington County judge candidates debate in Springdale. Candidates for Washington County judge participated in a debate in Springdale, discussing population growth and infrastructure.
University Auto And Tire opens second location in Elkins. Fayetteville-based University Auto and Tire has opened its second location in Elkins after acquiring a 6,500-square-foot vehicle maintenance shop.
Perrodin Supply Co. announces artists for Spring Creek exhibition. Perrodin Supply Co. has announced the artists who will be featured in its month-long exhibition celebrating Springdale's Spring Creek.
Rogers to host garden alchemy: herbs for home & Well-Being event. The city of Rogers will host a 'Garden Alchemy: Herbs for Home & Well-Being' event on October 10, exploring Victorian herbs.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 29, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville will celebrate the grand opening of a new trail tunnel near the Walmart Campus this week.
Bentonville to open new trail tunnel. The city of Bentonville will cut the ribbon this week on a new trail tunnel near the Walmart Campus, following multiple years of construction.
Square 2 Square Bike Ride returns to Bentonville. The Square 2 Square Bike Ride will conclude in downtown Bentonville this fall, marking its first return since 2023.
Square 2 Square bike ride to use Razorback Greenway on October 3. The Square 2 Square bike ride will take place on the Razorback Greenway on October 3, connecting Downtown Fayetteville and Downtown Bentonville.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee agenda: Committee to discuss its organization, duties, and authority. This discussion would clarify what matters the Traffic Safety & Signage Committee can consider and may lead to recommendations for the City Council, potentially affecting how traffic and signage issues are addressed in the city.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Lowell daycare site sells for $9.3 million. A 40,000-square-foot daycare building in Lowell, located near Interstate 49, recently sold for $9.3 million.
Rogers apartment complex sells for $51.85 million. The Fitzroy Grove, a 250-unit luxury apartment complex east of Interstate 49 in Rogers, recently sold for $51.85 million.
Bentonville housing development targets teacher needs. McAuley Place, a new housing development in Bentonville, is designed to help teachers afford to live in the area and save for homeownership.
Bentonville remains first in Arkansas Sports Media Poll. The Bentonville Tigers maintained their unbeaten record and top position in the latest Arkansas Sports Media Poll.
UA power group launches as new research institute. The University of Arkansas officially launched a new overarching research institute for electronics systems on Monday.
Walmart AMP seeks collector ticket designs. The Walmart AMP is holding a contest for collector ticket designs for its 2027 season.
Child care aware of NWA discusses early childhood education. A nonprofit organization, Child Care Aware of NWA, brought together advocates and providers to discuss solutions for childcare access in Arkansas.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 28, 2026
item.description:
Benton County has lifted its burn ban, which had been in effect since August.
Benton County lifts burn ban. Benton County's fire marshal has lifted the county's burn ban, which had been active since August.
Tractor Supply Co. and freddy’s frozen custard & steakburgers to open in lowell. Lowell is set to gain a new fast food restaurant and a Tractor Supply Co. following the approval of development plans last week.
New affordable apartment complex opens in Bentonville. A new workforce housing community officially opened its doors in Bentonville on September 25.
Bienvenue Restaurant moves to Pinnacle Hills. Bienvenue Restaurant, a European-inspired establishment, recently opened in the former Theo’s Rogers location at 3300 S. Market Street, Suite 100, in Rogers.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would cut the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from 1% to 0.5%, potentially making dining out slightly less expensive.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission Work Session agenda: Commission to consider splitting a lot at 44 Watson Drive. This proposed lot split, Case LSP-2026-67100, would divide Parcel 16-78005-010 into multiple parcels. The applicant is Troy Currens.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve buying a new John Deere tractor for the Street Department. This resolution would authorize the purchase of a new John Deere 5075M utility tractor with a rotary cutter for $63,860.36, which the Street Department would use for maintenance.
Harps Food Stores announces promotions. Will McDoniel has been promoted from meat and seafood category manager to director of AI strategy and innovation at Springdale-based Harps Food Stores.
Symphony of Northwest Arkansas to open mainstage season on October 3. The Symphony of Northwest Arkansas will begin its mainstage season on October 3 with “Rites of Renewal: The Firebird.”
Yuna nishamura wins NW Arkansas Championship. Yuna Nishamura won the 20th Walmart Northwest Arkansas Championship presented by P&G, marking her first LPGA victory.
Sheep Dog Impact Assistance takes over Veterans Wall of honor care. Veterans in Bella Vista celebrated a new chapter for the Veterans Wall of Honor as Sheep Dog Impact Assistance assumes responsibility for the memorial's care.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 27, 2026
item.description:
The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. This event is part of the Big Sugar Classic week.
Centerton food pantry closes after 15 years. A Centerton food pantry has closed after 15 years of operation. The pantry distributed over 1.8 million pounds of food to more than 92,000 individuals.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would reduce the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from 1% to 0.5%. This is the second reading of the ordinance.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission Work Session agenda: Commission to consider a lot split at 44 Watson Drive. This proposal would divide Parcel 16-78005-010 at 44 Watson Drive into multiple lots, if approved.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve purchasing a new tractor for the Street Department. The city is asked to approve a contract for $63,860.36 to purchase a new John Deere 5075M utility tractor with a rotary cutter for use by the Street Department.
Fayetteville Falltoberfest returns October 4. Fayetteville Falltoberfest will return on October 4, featuring German traditions, local music, art, food, and a dog pageant.
Northwest Arkansas Book Fest held at Walton Arts Center. The fourth annual Northwest Arkansas Book Fest took place at the Walton Arts Center. The event featured a full day of activities for readers of all ages.
Experts suggest diversifying Northwest Arkansas employers for growth. Experts suggest that Northwest Arkansas should diversify its employer base beyond its four major companies to maintain rapid regional growth.
Bikes, Blues & BBQ offers more than just biking events. The CEO of the Rogers-Lowell Chamber stated that Bikes, Blues & BBQ is not exclusively for bikers. The event also offers music and food for attendees.
Arkansas classical theatre presents Poe production. The Arkansas Classical Theatre is returning with a unique production based on the works of Edgar Allan Poe.
Centerton hosts NWA Emergency Preparedness Fair. Centerton hosted the NWA Emergency Preparedness Fair, where residents learned about safety. The event included participation from the Centerton Police Department, Centerton Fire Department, and Mercy Life Health.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 26, 2026
item.description:
The Arkansas Community Foundation launched a new program with a $10 million grant to address food insecurity in the state.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would reduce the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from 1% to 0.5%. This is the second reading of Ordinance No. 2017-15.
On the Bella Vista Planning Commission Work Session agenda: Commission to consider splitting a lot at 44 Watson Drive. This proposed lot split, Case LSP-2026-67100, would divide Parcel 16-78005-010 into multiple parcels. The applicant is Troy Currens.
Arkansas Community Foundation launches $10 million food insecurity fund. The Arkansas Community Foundation, in cooperation with the Walmart Foundation, announced a five-year initiative to address food insecurity, anchored by a $10 million grant from the Walmart Foundation.
McAuley Place development to welcome first residents in October. The McAuley Place development in Bentonville, which aims to offer affordable living options for teachers, will see its first residents move in next month.
Arkansas Department of Transportation to remove political signs from right-of-ways. The Arkansas Department of Transportation reminded candidates and their supporters that placing campaign signs on highway right-of-ways is unlawful and the department will remove them.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Walmart CEO addresses rumors about digital labels and AI pricing. Walmart CEO John Furner is pushing back on rumors regarding the retail giant's new pricing technology and its use of digital labels and AI.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 25, 2026
item.description:
The Benton County Quorum Court approved the creation of a fund for the Sheriff's Office's partnership with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement.
Benton county Quorum court approves fund for ICE program. The Benton County Quorum Court approved the creation of a fund for the Sheriff's Office's partnership with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement through its 287(g) Program.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would reduce the tax you pay on prepared food and beverages from 1% to 0.5%. This is the second reading of the ordinance.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve purchase of a new tractor for the Street Department. The city is asked to approve a contract for $63,860.36 to purchase a new John Deere 5075M utility tractor with a rotary cutter for use by the Street Department.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to approve appointment to the bella vista library advisory board. The Mayor's appointment of Julie Driver Grau to the Bella Vista Library Advisory Board would be approved, filling a term ending December 31, 2030.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville as part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Fayetteville school board renames performing arts facility. The Fayetteville School District's Performing Arts Center has been renamed in honor of longtime educator Warren Rosenaur.
Fayetteville park reopens after $1 million in improvements. Bryce Davis Park in Fayetteville reopened after the completion of approximately $1 million in park improvements.
Bentonville's Arkade adds 14 startup businesses. Bentonville's Arkade added 14 startup businesses in its first year.
Bentonville nonprofit advances in NASA challenge. Bentonville-based nonprofit research organization Autonomic Resilience Collective advanced to the final stage of a NASA challenge to design a food system for Mars.
VIC Tech appoints Sarah Goforth as chief growth officer. VIC Technology Venture Development, a Fayetteville-based company, named Sarah Goforth as chief growth officer and managing director.
Heartland Whole health launches rural health initiative. A Northwest Arkansas-based nonprofit, Heartland Whole Health, is starting an initiative to address the gap in healthcare access for millions of Americans in rural areas.
Crystal bridges to host Indigenous Arts symposium. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art will host an Indigenous Arts Symposium next month, featuring Indigenous artists and scholars.
Siloam Springs 'Twin Springs' landmark undergoing construction. A downtown Siloam Springs landmark, 'Twin Springs,' which has been closed to the public for over two decades, is undergoing renovation.
Fayetteville school construction projects on schedule. Ongoing Fayetteville School District projects, including Woodland Junior High, are expected to be completed on schedule.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 24, 2026
item.description:
Brandom Gengelbach will step down as president and CEO of the Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce on October 31.
Brandom Gengelbach to leave Bentonville chamber leadership. Brandom Gengelbach will step down as president and CEO of the Bentonville Area Chamber of Commerce on October 31, three years after being hired to lead the organization.
Bentonville City Council approves grants for road projects. The Bentonville City Council approved grants to partially fund several planned infrastructure projects in the city.
Bentonville City Council approves new artificial intelligence policy. The Bentonville City Council approved new guidelines for the city's use of artificial intelligence to comply with Arkansas state law.
UL Solutions expands testing at Lowell Retail Center of Excellence. UL Solutions expanded its Retail Center of Excellence in Lowell to include apparel and textiles testing, adding to its existing testing of furniture, toys, and electronics.
Updates provided on Bentonville overpass projects. A Bentonville City Council meeting included status updates on projects designed to improve traffic movement across Interstate 49.
Combined sales tax revenue up in four Northwest Arkansas cities. Bentonville, Fayetteville, Rogers, and Springdale reported a combined monthly sales tax revenue of $9.965 million in September, an increase of 2.35%.
Circle of life to acquire Washington Regional Hospice. Circle of Life will acquire Washington Regional Hospice and purchase the Willard Walker Hospice Home in Fayetteville.
Pay-what-you-can bookshop reopens in downtown Springdale. A nonprofit pay-what-you-can bookshop reopened in downtown Springdale, allowing readers to take books for free or pay what they can.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
Centerton food pantry to close after 15 years. The Centerton Food Pantry will close its doors after serving the community for 15 years.
Proposed waste management merger faces challenges in Benton County. Merger negotiators were informed that combining Northwest Arkansas' two solid waste districts faces an uphill climb in Benton County.
Lasang Pinoy restaurant in Rogers makes 50-best list. Lasang Pinoy, a Filipino restaurant in Rogers, represents Arkansas on the New York Times' 2026 list of America's Best Restaurants.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 23, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville City Council approved accepting over $5 million in grants for transportation projects.
Bentonville city council approves accepting over $5 million in transportation grants. The Bentonville City Council approved accepting two grants totaling more than $5 million for transportation projects aimed at enhancing the city's transit infrastructure.
Rogers city council approves Mount hebron road rezoning. The Rogers City Council approved a rezoning for Mount Hebron Road, a decision that followed an earlier denial and left some residents disappointed.
Hotel Vin Rogers opens in Pinnacle Hills. A new hotel, Hotel Vin Rogers, has opened in the Pinnacle Hills area, representing an investment of over $72 million and featuring three food and beverage concepts, an outdoor pool, and more than 10,000 square feet of event space.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled to take place in Bentonville on October 11, 2026, as part of the Big Sugar Classic week.
XNA sees narrow dip in August outbound passenger traffic. Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) experienced its second year-over-year decrease in outbound passenger traffic in August, following two consecutive months of record-high enplanements.
Crystal Bridges announces $250,000 Don Tyson Prize recipient. Crystal Bridges has announced the recipient of the 2026 Don Tyson Prize for the Advancement of American Art, which awards $250,000.
Boys and Girls Club of Benton County to offer free dinner for children and teens. The Boys and Girls Club of Benton County will provide free dinner and snacks for children aged 6-18 starting next year.
NWA Food Bank receives donation to kick off Walmart NW Arkansas Championship week. The Northwest Arkansas Food Bank received a joint donation of $20,000 and 40,000 pounds of protein from Walmart and Tyson Foods to mark the start of the 20th Walmart Northwest Arkansas Championship.
Centerton run to support foster children on October 10. Schuber Mitchell Homes is bringing the Love Running Home 5K & 1-Mile Fun Run to Centerton on October 10, an event designed to support children in foster care.
Acres.com releases housing market data product. Fayetteville-based land intelligence platform Acres.com has launched a new product that offers a nationwide view of housing market supply, pricing, and demand.
Springdale city council approves AI policy. The Springdale City Council has approved a policy to establish guidelines for the city's use of artificial intelligence, as mandated by Arkansas state law.
New York Times lists Rogers Filipino restaurant among U.S.' 50 best. Lasang Pinoy, a Filipino restaurant located at 719 W. Walnut St., Suite 104, in Rogers, was included in The New York Times' recently released list of America's Best Restaurants 2026.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 21, 2026
item.description:
The Siloam Springs city board will consider rezoning 13 acres for a 285-unit apartment development along Arkansas 16 during its October meeting.
Siloam Springs city board to consider rezoning for 285-unit apartment development. The Siloam Springs city Board of Directors is set to consider rezoning about 13 acres along Arkansas 16 to make way for an apartment development during its October meeting.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to consider reducing the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15 to reduce the tax residents pay on prepared food and beverages from one percent (1%) to one-half of one percent (0.5%).
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 201 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street than the current suburban single-family zoning permits, potentially leading to more varied housing options in the neighborhood.
On the Rogers City Council agenda: Council to amend Ordinance No. 24-04 regarding sewer revenue bond terms. This proposed amendment would revise the terms for the outstanding City of Rogers, Arkansas Sewer Revenue Bond, Series 2024, which could affect the city's financial obligations related to its sewer system.
On the Rogers Water Utilities Commission agenda: Commission to consider approving Resolution 26-25 for a 457(b) Deferred Compensation Plan. This proposed resolution would establish or modify a deferred compensation plan for employees, which could impact their retirement savings.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
University of Arkansas Medical Sciences opens new MS clinic in Fayetteville. The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences opened a new clinic for MS patients on September 18 in Fayetteville.
Bentonville School District receives highest a-ranking in the state. The Bentonville School District is leading the list of the top school districts in Arkansas with its highest A-ranking.
Arkansas Latinas en Bici hosts community bike ride in Bentonville. Arkansas Latinas en Bici, a local cycle group, hosted a community bike ride event throughout Bentonville on Sunday, September 20, encouraging community members to explore Northwest Arkansas.
UAMS hosts Girlology session for puberty education in Fayetteville. The University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences (UAMS) hosted a 'Girlology' informational session for young girls navigating puberty on Sunday in Fayetteville.
Northwest Arkansas cattle ranch expands operations. The 808 Ranch, located 15 minutes from downtown Bentonville, is expanding its operations and adding technology.
Arkansas basketball SEC-ACC challenge game times announced. The Razorbacks men's team will face North Carolina at 6:30 p.m. Central in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, while the women's team will play Wake Forest at 8 p.m. Central in Fayetteville.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 20, 2026
item.description:
Bentonville's City Council and Finance Committee will meet on September 22 to discuss various city matters.
On the Bella Vista City Council agenda: Council to reduce the prepared food and beverage tax rate. This proposed ordinance would amend Ordinance No. 2017-15 to decrease the tax on prepared food and beverages from one percent (1%) to one-half of one percent (0.5%). This change would mean residents pay less tax on prepared food and beverage purchases.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone 201 SW E Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family to T3.1, Neighborhood Edge. This proposed change would allow for a different type of development at 201 SW E Street than the current suburban single-family zoning permits, potentially leading to more varied housing options in the neighborhood.
On the Bentonville Finance Committee agenda: Committee to accept a $185,605 grant for the John DeShields Trail design and bidding. This would fund the design and bidding documents for trail improvements along the John DeShields Trail corridor between NE J Street and E Central Avenue.

Heat advisory issued for Benton county. The National Weather Service has issued a Heat Advisory for Benton County until 7:00 PM CDT today, September 6. Heat index values are expected to reach up to 109 degrees.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee - Changed Due to Labor Day Holiday agenda: Girls on the Run Fall Celebratory 5K on November 14th. The race will use the same route as last year and run from 7am to 12pm on November 14th, 2026, with the race beginning at 8:15am. Roads along the route will be affected during that time.
Bentonville Schools Board of education to meet September 15. The Bentonville Schools Board of Education has scheduled a meeting for September 15, 2026. An agenda for the meeting has not yet been posted.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. The event is part of Big Sugar Classic week.
Haag Brown commercial adds marketing leader to Northwest Arkansas office. Alley Harjo has joined real estate developer Haag Brown Commercial's Northwest Arkansas office. Harjo will serve as a marketing and creative leader for the company.
Drought conditions may impact autumn foliage in Northwest Arkansas. Autumn foliage in Northwest Arkansas may be less colorful this year if drought conditions persist. The lack of vibrant leaves could also affect tourism.
Washington Regional recognized on becker's list. Washington Regional has been named to a list compiled by Becker's.
America's Car-Mart approaches creditor deadline. Rogers-based America's Car-Mart faces a deadline set by its creditors to meet financial metrics. Failure to meet these metrics could result in a default on its loans.
NWACC's brightwater to offer free food training. Northwest Arkansas Community College's Brightwater culinary school will offer free food training. This opportunity is made possible through a grant from the Walton Family Foundation.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 5, 2026
item.description:
A heat advisory is in effect for Benton County until 7:00 PM CDT on September 5.
Heat advisory issued for Benton County. The National Weather Service in Tulsa, Oklahoma, issued a heat advisory for Benton County until 7:00 PM CDT on September 5. The advisory is in effect for multiple counties in Arkansas and Oklahoma.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to rezone property at 405 NW 5th Street. This would change the zoning of the property from suburban single-family to a neighborhood node classification, which could allow for different types of development than single-family homes.
On the Bentonville Traffic Safety and Signage Committee - Changed Due to Labor Day Holiday agenda: Girls on the Run Fall Celebratory 5K to be held on November 14, 2026. This item provides information about the Girls on the Run NWA Fall Celebratory 5K, which would use the same route as last year and take place from 7 AM to 12 PM, with the race beginning at 8:15 AM.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to approve a change order for the 12-inch water main reroute project. This would approve an additional $22,955.00 for the water main reroute project, covering costs for relocated water meters, fence removal, temporary gate installation, a final cut and cap, and a culvert addition. The original contract price was $694,210.99.
Arkansas Department of Transportation opens $400 million in highways. The Arkansas Department of Transportation opened $400 million in interstate-style highway projects in Northwest Arkansas. This includes a new stretch of Interstate 42 and a direct connector to Northwest Arkansas National Airport.
Walmart to deliver dunkin’ drinks and food. Walmart will begin delivering Dunkin’ drinks and food.
Little Sugar MTB scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville. The event is part of Big Sugar Classic week.

item.title: Bentonville Daily — September 4, 2026
item.description:
The Cave Springs Planning Commission approved a site development plan for the city's first Walmart Neighborhood Market and gas station.
Cave Springs Planning Commission approves Walmart Neighborhood Market plan. The Cave Springs Planning Commission approved a site development plan for a Walmart Neighborhood Market and gas station, moving the city closer to having its first such store.
Benton County Planning board of appeals overturns cell tower denial. The Benton County Planning Board of Appeals overturned a previous decision, allowing a proposed 150-foot-tall telecommunications tower to be built.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to consider rezoning 405 NW 5th Street. This proposed ordinance would change the zoning of the property at 405 NW 5th Street from R-1, Suburban Single-Family, to T4.2, Neighborhood Node, which could allow for different types of development than currently permitted.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to accept a $2,000,000 grant for Vaughn Road improvements. This resolution would authorize the acceptance of a $2,000,000 grant to help fund the construction of the Hwy 12/279 Intersection Improvements project.
On the Bentonville City Council agenda: Council to approve a change order for the 12-inch water main reroute project. This resolution would approve Change Order #1 for the 12-inch Water Main Reroute project, adding $22,955.00 to the original contract price of $694,210.99 for work including water meter relocation, fence removal, and a culvert addition.
Tyson Foods lowers 2026 revenue guidance. Tyson Foods Inc. lowered its revenue growth guidance for 2026 due to significant margin pressure from the cattle industry.
7 Brew acquires 73 Salad and Go locations for $143.2 million. Springdale-based 7 Brew won a bankruptcy auction to acquire 73 locations of the Salad and Go chain for $143.2 million.
Crystal bridges museum announces new jewelry and gemstone exhibition. Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art announced an upcoming exhibition that will feature historically significant jewelry and gemstones.
Walmart senior advisor Jane Ewing to join Nike. Jane Ewing, a senior advisor and executive board member for ethics and compliance in Walmart's China operations, is leaving the company to join Nike.
Northwest and central Arkansas metros lead state job growth. Northwest Arkansas and central Arkansas continue to be the primary areas for job growth in the state, with year-over-year job gains of 2.6% and 1.3% respectively in July.
Little Sugar MTB race scheduled for October 11, 2026. The Little Sugar MTB mountain-bike race, part of Big Sugar Classic week, is scheduled for October 11, 2026, in Bentonville.
